children: Amazon.com said Wednesday that it plans to raise the minimum starting pay for its full-time core staff. The move comes with a price tag of more than $1.5 billion for the e-commerce company.

The minimum starting pay for Amazon's U.S. full-time core operations roles will rise to $20 an hour, an increase of $1 an hour. The company said its minimum starting pay has increased more than 17% in the past three years.
Amazon said the latest increase means average pay for U.S. core staff will be $24 an hour, or more than $32 per hour with benefits added in.

Amazon also said it would introduce new benefits for employees, including lifetime banking services, and additional discounts on groceries. Existing Amazon benefits include free membership in its Prime subscription service for eligible employees, and healthcare for as low as $5 a week with $5 copays.
The company also on Wednesday announced a pay increase for workers in the U.K., having made a similar announcement for mainland European workers last week.

Amazon didn't disclose how many employees would be affected by the changes. As of the end of 2025, Amazon employed around 1.58 million full-time and part-time employees. At the start of this year, Amazon said it would cut 16,000 jobs, as part of its largest-ever corporate layoffs.
Amazon shares were down 0.2% in early trading.
